line: e4 Nf6 e5 Nd5 d4 d6 c4 Nb6 f4 dxe5 fxe5 Nc6 Be3 Bf5 Nc3
teaches: Develop in the order that keeps an answer ready for the opponent's most annoying jump — a knight coming beside your queenside pawns is only a problem while the rook behind them is still at home.
explains: Develop in the order that keeps an answer ready for the opponent's most annoying jump. A knight landing beside your queenside pawns is only a problem while the rook behind them sits at home — so the knight comes to c3, holding d5 and b5 and clearing the rook's path to the c-file if that knight ever hops in. It answers a move that hasn't been played yet.
